subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: Should ordinary skill-publish source flags be retained as clearly unverified public attribution, deprecated and rejected, or upgraded through a new server-verified GitHub publishing workflow?
rationale: The choice defines both a public CLI/API contract and the security meaning of provenance, so implementation cannot safely infer the intended policy from existing code.

options.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
options.body: Retain the declarations separately from trusted provenance and visibly label them as publisher-provided and unverified.

options.title: Add Verified Publishing
options.body: Build server-side repository, commit, path, and content verification before CLI-published source can enter trusted provenance.

options.title: Deprecate Source Flags
options.body: Reject or remove the ambiguous skill-publish flags and document GitHub import as the only trusted source path.

recommendation.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
recommendation.body: Retain the declarations separately from trusted provenance and visibly label them as publisher-provided and unverified.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source implementation is the strongest available ownership signal for deciding this adjacent provenance contract.
